reason: The acceptance criteria checklist. All ten items must be traceable to code or to a named test, or reported as not implemented. Criteria 3 and 4 are the behaviour flip — verify both directions, not just the permissive one.

Verify the implementation matches the decision: Class A derived from ENDPOINT_SUFFIX prefixes (not hand-listed), Class B still a hard reject with protocol attribution, ?/# untouched, and the post-strip https://<non-empty host> re-check present.

Documentation-consistency check: the failure matrix, the Good/Bad cases and the Tests Required list must describe the new behaviour. A spec row still saying a /v1 anthropic root is rejected is a defect in this change, not a leftover.

Security check: grep every new log line and error message for anything that could carry the URL, model or key. The base-URL messages are the case that makes this absolute — a gateway base URL can hold a key in a query string.

Verify no ValueError escapes config.py and that load_settings still raises only RuntimeError. A ValueError from the new post-strip check would propagate out of run_sync, which promises never to raise.

Terminology check: code, comments and docs must use the glossary's words. Classifier Endpoint is still always an API root; only how it is derived changed. Flag any comment that now claims LLM_BASE_URL is itself the root.
The forbidden-pattern table plus the gating commands: uv run pytest backend/tests, uv run ruff check backend/, uv run ruff format --check backend/.
Verify llm/ stayed stdlib-only with no logger added, that llm/__init__.py still does not re-export adapter modules, and that get_adapter's lazy in-function import is intact.
